content: The George Foundation (TGF) is a non-governmental organization (NGO) established in 1995, headquartered in Bangalore, India. It was founded by Dr. Abraham M. George, a successful entrepreneur in the United States who returned to India to initiate various humanitarian projects. The foundation's mission is to alleviate poverty, promote health and environmental sustainability, and strengthen democratic institutions and values in India. Its primary focus is on rural areas in Tamil Nadu (mainly in the Krishnagiri district) and Karnataka, serving over 16,000 people across 17 villages. These communities are among the poorest in the country, with over 70% of the population living on less than one dollar per day, and high rates of illiteracy, malnutrition, female infanticide, and bonded labor. Projects Alleviation of Poverty TGF's poverty alleviation initiatives aim to improve education and healthcare delivery, provide essential amenities such as proper housing and water resources, and create employment opportunities to sustain rural families. Shanti Bhavan Boarding School: Shanti Bhavan was founded on the belief that impoverished children possess the same innate abilities as their more privileged peers. The project assumes that with access to quality education and consistent encouragement, these children can achieve their full potential and become productive members of society. Established in September 1997 with 48 students, the school is located in Baliganapalli, an impoverished area in the Krishnagiri district of Tamil Nadu. Students are selected based on family income (focusing on the poorest families) and intelligence (targeting children deemed capable of succeeding in the school). TGF plans to expand the school to accommodate 336 students. The campus is designed to be as self-sufficient as possible, with ground wells, water storage tanks, a horticultural garden, orchards, and a bakery. Solar power meets much of the institution's energy needs. The program spans from preschool to twelfth grade and is accredited by the Council for the Indian School Certificate Examination in New Delhi. The curriculum is rigorous, covering a wide range of subjects, with formal instruction in language and mathematics during the first three years. English is the medium of instruction, while Hindi and Tamil are introduced by the fourth year. Students are also encouraged to explore interests in sports, arts, music, and drama. In addition to Shanti Bhavan, TGF is working to improve public schools in the area, where the quality of education is generally poor due to a lack of teachers for all grades. Community Development Program: This program operates in the 17 villages surrounding Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. According to TGF, the initiative aims to bring significant improvements to the lives of the entire population served within a 10-year period starting in 2006. The program focuses on creating livelihood opportunities, education and skills training, healthcare, housing, water management, infrastructure development, and social progress. Agri-Business Training Centre Women’s Empowerment: The Women’s Empowerment Project trains women in farming techniques. Poor women from Tamil Nadu and Karnataka are provided with a quarter-acre of land, supplies, equipment, and training in cottage and cooperative farming. As of 2007, the project was still in its preparatory stages. Tillany Fine Arts Museum & Gallery: Built in 2000 near Shanti Bhavan, this 15,000-square-foot air-conditioned facility is designed in a contemporary style. Once fully operational, it will provide poor artists with exposure to global artwork, free access to tools for creating their own art, and support in promoting and marketing their creations. Art displayed at the museum will be sold, with 40% of the proceeds going to the artist. Protection of Health and the Environment Baldev Medical and Community Centre: This center serves the 17 villages in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, treating approximately 30 patients daily. It provides home visits, health checks for children at the government-run Deeverapalli school, and health education classes. The center also conducts annual sanitation clean-ups in the villages, maintaining drainage systems and latrines. It is equipped to handle infectious and parasitic diseases, chronic and degenerative conditions, respiratory infections, gastrointestinal issues, malnutrition-related ailments, skin diseases, and emergencies such as food poisoning, injuries, and childbirth complications. Serious cases are referred to nearby city hospitals. Multi-specialty clinics are held periodically, offering services in obstetrics and gynecology, pediatrics, dermatology, ophthalmology, ENT, and dentistry. Patients are charged nominal fees based on their ability to pay. Lead Poisoning Prevention and Treatment: Project Lead-Free was launched in 1997 to screen blood lead levels in children, pregnant women in urban areas, and workers in hazardous occupations. In February 1999, TGF organized a three-day international conference on lead poisoning in Bangalore, co-sponsored by the World Health Organization, the World Bank, the US Environmental Protection Agency, and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The conference proceedings were compiled into a book, Lead Poisoning Prevention and Treatment: Implementing a National Program in Developing Countries, and a white paper was presented to policymakers in developing nations. The findings from blood screenings and conference discussions influenced the Indian government’s decision to introduce unleaded gasoline nationwide in 2000. In 2003, TGF partnered with St. John’s Academy of Health Sciences in Bangalore to establish the National Referral Centre for Lead Poisoning Prevention in India (NRCLPI). The center raises public awareness about lead poisoning, assists polluting industries in implementing remedial measures, and confirms blood lead cases referred by clinics and hospitals across the country. NRCLPI is currently conducting follow-up studies on blood lead levels, lead additives in petrol, harmful metals in vegetables and house dust, and pathways of lead poisoning and contamination. Improved Governance Indian Institute of Journalism & New Media (IIJNM): Founded in 2001 by TGF and Sri Adichunchanagiri Mahasthana, IIJNM’s curriculum was developed in collaboration with Columbia University’s Graduate School of Journalism. The institute focuses on teaching the craft and ethics of journalism. TGF views the school as a means to improve governance by fostering a strong and independent press. IIJNM has introduced television and radio courses and is now ranked among the top three journalism colleges in India by Business World magazine. Centres for Studies in Emerging Critical Issues: This initiative brings together prominent individuals from India and abroad to address economic, social, and environmental challenges facing developing nations. The findings are presented as papers and lectures. Milestones Since its inception, TGF has significantly improved the economic status of the communities it serves. Hundreds of individuals, particularly poor women, now earn steady incomes, enabling them to support their families, access healthcare, repay debts, and escape bonded labor. Many others have benefited indirectly. In education, Shanti Bhavan School has gained global recognition for its mission and achievements, as highlighted in Thomas Friedman’s book The World is Flat. TGF’s support for government schools has led to higher attendance and academic standards, especially among girls. For example, the Deverapalli government school was recognized as the best in the district in 2005. The outreach program of the Baldev Medical Centre has reduced malnutrition, improved sanitation, and decreased maternal and infant mortality rates in the villages it serves. The lead testing initiative in major Indian cities and the subsequent international conference persuaded the government and major oil companies to eliminate lead from gasoline in 2000. NRCLPI is now the leading institution in India for promoting measures to prevent lead poisoning. IIJNM has increased its enrollment and expanded its curriculum, solidifying its position as a premier journalism school in India.
